evidence.note: Front-loaded orientation: inspected one config JSON and one dataset sample per protocol before coding — establishes a per-protocol frame that structures the subsequent build.

Built a dedicated prototype/test script per protocol in /tmp (test_sts, test_cls, test_clst, test_pc, test_summ) — each protocol's logic was verified in isolation before integration, which is stronger than an implicit 'this type works' checkpoint.
Retrieval milestone treated as its own sub-goal: iterated repeatedly on pytrec_eval cutoff/truncation semantics (recall, MRR@k) in isolated scripts until satisfied before folding into evaluate.py.

After integration, ran structural checks per representative task (run_eval on sts_01, retrieval_08) and noted 'all six task types passed structural checks' — an explicit per-type done-gate, but the gate is structural/'it ran', not tied to matching an external reference number.

Later phase handled shared concerns (offline model loading, timeouts, results.json shape, clustering edge cases) as separate sub-goals; intention to 'validate numerical correctness' appears (step 51/84) but exit gates remain structural rather than tolerance-against-gold per milestone.

reasoning: The agent clearly decomposed the build protocol-by-protocol, prototyping each of the six protocols in dedicated test scripts and verifying representative single tasks before fanning out — this exceeds the level-5 'implicit this-type-works checkpoint' by giving each protocol genuine isolated verification. However, the milestone done-conditions are anchored to structural passes and 'it computes' rather than to explicit external reference numbers (leaderboard/tolerance) per protocol, and there is no evidence of sequencing milestones by risk (e.g., dedicating extra budget to the trap-heavy clustering/pair-classification gates against gold). That places it between the level-5 and level-8 anchors, at a 6.
